note:
Round 2 of the SELFIE variant for the three clinical-result blocks on /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research - templates/page.research-argireline.json, section `key_findings`, blocks f1, f2, f3. Malcolm, 2026-08-25: more of the selfie and home-made style with everyday, normal, less attractive models. All earlier waves kept.

⚠️ THIS WAVE CANNOT MEET RULE 1, AND THE REASON IS BILLING, NOT A CHOICE. nbp_pro and nbp_flash both return HTTP 429 - and the message is NOT a daily rate limit, it is "Your billing account has exceeded its monthly spending cap". Probed directly on 2026-08-26 before this wave ran, both models, both 429. So the Gemini pair is unavailable until the cap is raised or the month rolls over, which is a spending decision and Malcolm's to make. A previous session's note that the quota "resets daily" was wrong and is corrected here. Luma additionally refuses this brief family with HTTP 422 - five times now - because it has no negative-prompt field and the negative list folds into its prompt body.
That leaves seedream, gpt_image and flux2. To recover some of the lost variety, CANDIDATES ARE RAISED FROM 2 TO 4: seedream 4 + gpt_image 4 + flux2 1 (it returns one per call regardless) gives about 9 per slot against the usual 11. NOTE THE ABSENCE WHEN JUDGING - nbp_flash has won most previous rounds on this brief, so this batch is not a fair engine comparison, only a fair look at the direction.

THREE FAULTS FROM SELFIE r1, EACH FIXED HERE:
  * flux2 laid a stock-photo style WATERMARK across the top of its f1 candidate. `no watermark text, no stock photo watermark, no printed text overlay, no logo overlay` added. It is a documented flux2 trait, so check its frames at full size regardless.
  * nbp_pro put a PHONE in the corner of the frame despite `no phone in frame`. Negatives alone were not enough, so the prompt BODY now states it positively and at length: the phone, its edge, its case, any hand or finger, any mirror or reflection never appear, and her arm is entirely outside the frame.
  * seedream cast an EAST ASIAN woman against the Caucasian brief. Ethnicity now leads the casting paragraph in the prompt body rather than sitting only in the negatives, and the negatives name the misfires explicitly.

THE DIRECTION, AND WHY IT IS THE MOST BELIEVABLE VERSION SO FAR. A studio pair invites the question "who lit this and why" - nobody photographs themselves that way at home. A phone snapshot answers it. The framing device does the work the polish was fighting: crooked framing, wrong indoor white balance, shadow noise, a wide lens enlarging the nose, eyes aimed at the screen rather than the lens. It also solves the session-variance problem properly - r3 and the full-face wave could only ask for two studio keys differing "a little", which is small and artificial, whereas a kitchen fluorescent versus a parked car in daylight is a large and completely natural difference. This round pushes the settings further apart than r1 did: kitchen at night vs a car; a dim bedroom vs an open front door; a bathroom flash vs an overcast garden.

CARRIED OVER UNCHANGED:
  * THE HONESTY DEVICE: the number and position of the lines is the same in both panels, NO LINE MAY DISAPPEAR, only depth and shadow change. f1 about half, f2 about a third, f3 the smallest but still visible.
  * ITS SELFIE EXTENSION: she must not come back better GROOMED. The easiest way for an engine to "improve" an unglamorous woman is to tidy her - makeup, styled hair, evened tone, a slimmer face. Each after-panel names what must stay: regrowth and sun damage on f1, acne scarring and grey roots and oily skin on f2, sunken cheeks and sallow tone and thin hair on f3. CHECK THIS FIRST ON EVERY CANDIDATE.
  * NO CAPTION-SHAPED NOUNS. nbp_pro drew "FIRST VISIT"/"FOLLOW-UP" in r3 and seedream drew "VISIT" in the full-face wave, each time because the word was in the prompt. The word visit appears nowhere in this brief - verified by count before running, as in selfie r1, which came back clean.
  * THREE NEW WOMEN, none used in any previous wave.
  * ⚠️ PALETTE: a selfie cannot carry Acetyl's Pearl grey D8D6D4 studio ground without destroying the premise, so these three blocks would lose the page's scene colour. Real cost, stated not hidden.
  * ⚠️ SITE OF MEASUREMENT: all three trials measured the PERIORBITAL region, so a full-face frame shows more than the site measured. Block copy and alt text must not imply otherwise.
  * ⚠️ RENDER SIZE: 660px desktop / 350px mobile, split in two, so each face renders about 330px / 175px. Fine lines sit at the edge of visibility and the percentage plate carries much of the message. Judge at render size.

CLASS B, no references. Square 2048x2048, each panel a 1:2 portrait.

slots.title: f1 · Wang 2013 — 48.9% anti-wrinkle efficacy vs 0% placebo, 4 weeks  —  selfie r2
slots.prompt:
Two ordinary front-camera phone selfies of THE SAME WOMAN, taken WEEKS APART at home, placed side by side to fill one square frame edge to edge: TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH meeting at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre. Each panel is a tall portrait. The left panel is the earlier one, the right panel is the later one.

THESE ARE AMATEUR SNAPSHOTS, NOT PHOTOGRAPHY. She holds the phone out at arm's length and uses its front camera, so: the wide lens sits close to her face and slightly enlarges her nose while pushing her ears back; the framing is crooked and off-centre; the focus is imperfect; there is visible digital noise in the shadows; and the white balance is wrong in the ordinary way a phone gets it wrong indoors. Her near shoulder is raised a little because her arm is up.

THE PHONE ITSELF IS NEVER VISIBLE. No phone, no phone edge, no case, no hand and no fingers appear anywhere in either panel, and there is no mirror and no reflection. Her arm is entirely outside the frame. Nothing in either picture is styled or lit on purpose.

HER WHOLE FACE IS IN VIEW IN BOTH PANELS - head and shoulders, the entire face from above the hairline to the collarbones, nothing cropped off. Both eyes, the nose, the whole mouth and the full jawline are visible. Her expression is flat, tired and self-conscious on both days, mouth closed, not smiling and not posing.

THESE ARE TWO SEPARATE OCCASIONS, NOT TWO COPIES OF ONE FRAME. Everything that identifies her stays the same, and everything a different day would change is different.

UNMISTAKABLY THE SAME WOMAN: the same face shape and jawline, the same nose, the same eye colour, the same brow shape, the same hair colour and cut, and her permanent marks - moles, freckles, sun spots, broken capillaries, old scarring - in the same places on her face.

CLEARLY DIFFERENT BETWEEN THE TWO OCCASIONS:
  * PLACE AND LIGHT - on the earlier day she is in a kitchen at night under a fluorescent ceiling strip, which throws a flat greenish light straight down on her and drops her eye sockets into shadow; on the later day she is sitting in a parked car in daylight, lit softly and coolly through the side window with the seat headrest behind her. The two pictures plainly were not taken in the same room or the same conditions.
  * HEAD POSITION - she holds the phone at a different height and angle each time, so the camera is above her eyeline on one day and below it on the other, her head is turned and tilted differently, and she sits differently in the frame.
  * EYE GAZE - on one day she is watching her own face on the screen, so her eyes aim slightly low and off to one side; on the other she looks more or less into the lens.
  * BACKGROUND - a completely different part of an ordinary home, plain and softly out of focus, and at a different brightness.
  * CLOTHES - a completely different everyday garment each time, a different colour and neckline - the sort of thing worn around the house.
  * HAIR - the same cut, unstyled, falling differently: a different parting, flatter on one day, strands out of place, one strand across her face in only one panel.

She must never stop being recognisably the same woman, and she must not appear older or younger, heavier or thinner, in one panel than the other.

SHE IS A WHITE EUROPEAN WOMAN, AND SHE IS ORDINARY-LOOKING RATHER THAN A MODEL. This matters more than anything else in the picture. Cast her the way a real person looks, not the way a beauty advertisement casts: she is about fifty-seven, with short grey-brown hair showing several centimetres of untinted regrowth at the parting, a long jowly face with heavy folds either side of the mouth, thin colourless lips, pale blue eyes under heavy hooded lids, and dry flaking patches beside the nostrils. Her neck is slack and her chest is heavily freckled and sun-damaged. Her features are asymmetric - one eye sits slightly lower than the other, her nose is not straight, and the two sides of her face do not match. She wears no makeup, her brows are untidy and unshaped, and her hair is unstyled and flat. Nothing about her is glamorous or photogenic, and neither picture makes any attempt to flatter her.

WHAT THE COMPARISON IS ABOUT, AND THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE TRUE: the number and position of the expression lines on her face is the same in both panels and NOT ONE OF THEM HAS DISAPPEARED. Her moles, freckles, scarring and broken capillaries are all still there in the same places. What has changed between the two occasions is only HOW DEEP the lines are. She has not been made younger, slimmer, prettier or better groomed - the same ordinary face is simply less deeply creased.

THE SKIN MUST HOLD UP AS REAL AND UNFLATTERED. Pores are clearly visible and vary in size and density by zone - open and obvious through the centre of the face and across the nose, finer at the temples and jaw - with several individual pores larger than their neighbours. Pigmentation is uneven and asymmetric, never mirrored from one side to the other. Fine pale vellus hairs catch the light along the jaw and upper lip. The skin is greasy and light-catching across the nose and forehead and dry at the outer cheeks. No makeup on either day, so her lips, lashes and brows are their own natural colour and her under-eye shadows are her own.

ON THE EARLIER DAY, in the LEFT panel, her expression lines are deeply set even with her face at rest: a fan of four or five creases spreading from the outer corner of each eye, three horizontal lines across the forehead, a pair of short vertical creases between the brows, and a deep fold running down from each side of the nose. In the hard overhead light each one holds a clear shadow along its length.

ON THE LATER DAY, in the RIGHT panel, EVERY ONE OF THOSE LINES IS STILL THERE, IN THE SAME PLACES AND THE SAME NUMBER, AND NOT ONE HAS DISAPPEARED. Each is about HALF as deep - the fold softer, the shadow it holds much lighter, its edges less sharply defined. The deep folds beside her mouth are still plainly visible. Her regrowth, freckling, sun damage and slack neck are exactly as they were.

A snapshot off a phone, not a photograph - slightly soft, slightly noisy, honest and completely unretouched.
